Generally, of course, a community would build its own Synagogue, or else depend on the charitable assistance of neighbours, or on private munificence. If this failed, they might meet for worship in a private dwelling, a sort of ‘Synagogue in the house.’ Comp. Philem. 2.

As a rule, synagogues were built at the expense of the congregation, though perhaps assisted by richer neighbours.
